Continuous variables: median [IQR] (Kruskal-Wallis). Categorical: n (%) (Chi-square or Fisher exact). 95% CIs for proportions (Wilson). "n too small" = group n < 10.
Table 2 — Outcomes Overall and by HF Phenotype
Outcomes include HF readmission, LV recovery, GDMT achievement and advanced-HF care.
Figure 1A — Kaplan-Meier All-Cause Mortality
Time from enrollment to death. Censored at last visit or analysis date. Log-rank p-value reported.

Time from enrollment to first readmission (Last_Admission). Patients without readmission censored.
GDMT Cascade — HFrEF
Step-by-step attrition: diagnosed → on ACEi/ARB/ARNI → +BB → +MRA → +SGLT2i → all four pillars → on ≥50% target dose → LV recovered.
Pillar Combination Profile
How many of the 4 pillars each HFrEF patient is on (0-4).
Dose-Titration Ladder
Among patients on each pillar, the % at ≥100%, 50-99%, <50% of target dose.
Longitudinal Trajectories
Mean ± 95% CI across visits 1-N. Stratified by HF phenotype.
KCCQ Change Distribution (Latest − Baseline)
Histogram. Vertical lines mark MCID (±5 pts) and large clinical change (±10 pts).
Guideline Benchmark Gaps — HFrEF GDMT
Our uptake vs published quality benchmarks (Get-With-The-Guidelines targets shown as red reference line). Negative gap = under-treatment.
Physician Variation — GDMT Completeness
Funnel plot: each dot = one physician. Lines = 95% and 99.8% control limits around overall mean. Dots outside limits = statistically significant outliers.
Past History / Comorbidity Co-occurrence Matrix
% of patients with each pair of comorbidities present together. Darker = higher co-occurrence.
Inotrope & MCS Utilization
Use of inotropes and mechanical circulatory support by support type.

ESC HF criteria for iron deficiency: ferritin <100 µg/L OR (100-300 + TSAT <20%). Treated = on iron therapy.
